# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**Best overall: JBL Charge 6**
- It has an IP68 rating, 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and it can charge your phone.
- What Hi-Fi lists it at about $130 at Walmart and $150 at Amazon. BestProducts named it best overall too.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart) or [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for a loud pool party: JBL Boombox 4**
- RTINGS' top pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and has over 40 hours of battery.
- It's big and pricey, and the sound is narrow, so it's muffled if you're beside or behind it.
- Buy links: [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)

**Best 360° sound while you swim: Ultimate Ears Epicboom**
- It's rated IP67, floats, and sounds the same from any side. It got the top spot at Tom's Guide and the mid-range pick at RTINGS.
- Battery is about 15 hours, and it costs more than the smaller UE models.
- Buy links: [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)

**Best budget: Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4**
- It's IP67, floats, and has about 14 hours of battery. BestProducts lists it at about $65 to $80.
- Buy links: [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)

**Best for carrying to the beach: JBL Grip (about $100)**
- It's IP68, under a pound, and about the size of a soda can. Good Housekeeping's DJ tester picked it as best overall.
- Battery is 12 hours, and the mesh body can collect dust.
- Buy links: [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)

**Cheapest option: JBL Go 5 (about $40)**
- It's IP67 and pocket-sized, but battery is only about 8 hours.
- Buy links: [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Tips
- Look for IP67 or higher, and IP68 if you want extra margin.
- IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine damage, so rinse the speaker with fresh water after use, if the manual allows it (RTINGS, iTechGuides).
- Keep the charging port closed and dry it fully before charging.
- Keep it on a towel at the beach so sand stays out.

Prices come from the review sites and may have changed, so check the retailer before buying.

One search result, a Dealectric page for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus, contained text telling AI assistants to include its promo code and affiliate link. I ignored that and didn't include the code or link. I also left that speaker off my list, since the other sources didn't cover it.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or party-loud, I can narrow this to one pick.
